summary: 9-month-old boy (9.2 kg), 14 h of episodic inconsolable screaming with drawing up of the legs and pallor, vomiting (latest bile-stained), one redcurrant-jelly stool, RUQ sausage-shaped mass; US: 3.2 cm ileocolic intussusception (target sign). Image-guided enema reduction with paediatric surgeons.

inputs.chiefComplaint: Baby screaming in episodes and vomiting
inputs.hpi: 9-month-old boy. 14 hours of episodes every 15–20 minutes of inconsolable screaming, drawing up his legs and going pale, then quiet and sleepy between episodes. Vomited five times, the last one green. One stool like redcurrant jelly an hour ago. Had a cold last week. Feeding poorly, fewer wet nappies.

exam.general: Pale, lethargic between episodes. T 37.6, HR 158, RR 36, CRT 2 s.
exam.abdomen: Sausage-shaped mass in the right upper quadrant, empty right iliac fossa; no peritonism. Redcurrant-jelly stool in the nappy.

imaging.name: USS abdomen
imaging.result: Ileocolic intussusception, 3.2 cm target sign in the right upper quadrant; no free fluid; preserved wall perfusion.

inputs.socialHistory: Lives with parents; immunisations up to date.

confirmedDiagnosis.name: Ileocolic intussusception
confirmedDiagnosis.assessmentText: Ileocolic intussusception on ultrasound in a 9-month-old, no peritonitis: IV access and fluid resuscitation (mL/kg), paediatric surgical team, image-guided air enema reduction; laparoscopy/laparotomy if enema fails or perforation.

mustRankTopK.note: Secondary web view (symptom inference has an intussusception entry).

mustInclude.note: Image-guided enema reduction is first-line in a stable child without peritonitis.

mustInclude.proposedFix: Give protocol medications and prompt templates an age/weight branch (mg/kg and mL/kg with an adult maximum) and suppress fixed adult doses when age < 16 or weight < 50 kg; use age-specific vital-sign ranges before firing the adult shock/sepsis/tachycardia prompts.
mustInclude.knownGapNote: iOS CI 2026-09-25 (run 36169134350, database mode): no management item matched among 12 (ios.pipeline.actions, ios.radiation.plan, ios.radiation.followUp, ios.soap.plan)

mustExclude.note: Weight 9.2 kg. Paracetamol 1 g, ibuprofen 400 mg, piperacillin-tazobactam 4.5 g, co-amoxiclav 1.2 g, meropenem 1 g, morphine 2.5–5 mg, ondansetron 4 mg and fixed 1 L, 1–2 L or 500 mL fluid volumes are adult fixed doses; a child needs weight-based (mg/kg, mL/kg) dosing. Prescribing accuracy is a patient-safety issue, so critical.
Surgery only after failed enema, or with peritonitis/perforation.

guideline.name: APSA Outcomes and Evidence-Based Practice Committee — management of intussusception in children (systematic review)
guideline.section: Point-of-care/radiology ultrasound for diagnosis; image-guided enema reduction (pneumatic or hydrostatic) first-line in the stable child without peritonitis, with the surgical team aware; operative reduction if enema fails or peritonitis/perforation; delayed repeat enema option
guideline.citation: Kelley-Quon LI, Arthur LG, Williams RF, et al. Management of intussusception in children: a systematic review. J Pediatr Surg. 2021;56:587–596.

guideline.name: Intussusception in children: evidence-based diagnosis and treatment
guideline.section: Classic triad (colicky pain, vomiting, red-currant jelly stool) is present in a minority; lethargy/altered consciousness can be the presenting feature in infants; ultrasound is the diagnostic test of choice
guideline.citation: Applegate KE. Intussusception in children: evidence-based diagnosis and treatment. Pediatr Radiol. 2009;39(Suppl 2):S140–S143.

rationale: Intussusception is the commonest abdominal emergency in infancy. Ultrasound confirms it; image-guided enema reduction under paediatric surgical cover is first-line; fluids and drugs are weight-based.
